The Senate had not acted on it as of the newest source. The TAKE IT DOWN Act (May 2025) deals with posting intimate images, not children's access.

happened: Congress passed a law in 2024 requiring TikTok to be sold or banned, and the Supreme Court upheld it on January 17, 2025. President Trump delayed enforcement several times. A deal moving TikTok's U.S. business into a joint venture controlled by American investors closed in January 2026; ByteDance kept 19.9%, and the venture licenses the app's algorithm from ByteDance.

key_dates.event: Supreme Court upholds the TikTok divest-or-ban law (TikTok v. Garland).

uncertain: Whether the deal fully meets the law's limits on ByteDance control, especially over the algorithm. Newest source is from January 2026.

happened: In April 2026 the FCC adopted rules, effective June 9, 2026, requiring a wide range of license holders to state whether they are owned or controlled by a foreign adversary and, if so, to disclose details. Ownership of 10 percent or more of equity by such parties is among the triggers. The FCC told its staff to set up how this information will be published. In October 2026 it sent the new reporting form (FCC Form 5655, about 18,000 expected filers) to OMB for approval.

happened: The July 2025 reconciliation law restored the FCC's spectrum auction authority through 2034. It requires auctions of at least 300 megahertz, including at least 100 megahertz in the 3.98-4.2 GHz band within two years, and requires NTIA to identify another 500 megahertz of federal spectrum for commercial use on a set schedule. In July 2026 the FCC adopted rules to auction the Upper C-band under that law.

happened: On June 6, 2025, the Commerce Department's NTIA issued a policy notice restructuring the $42.5 billion BEAD broadband grant program, which it calls the "Benefit of the Bargain" reforms. States had to rerun grant selections, open them to all technologies including satellite, and pick the lowest-cost option for each unserved location. In January 2026 NTIA held a listening session on how to use the money saved.

happened: On April 9, 2026, the White House Council on Environmental Quality issued guidance on creating, adopting and using categorical exclusions, which let low-impact projects skip detailed environmental reviews, replacing 2010 guidance. In April 2026 a broadband industry group asked the Agriculture Department, which runs the Forest Service, to adopt broadband exclusions under that guidance. A 2024 Bureau of Land Management rule, from before this administration, already set a 270-day target for deciding broadband applications.
